head: 2559613c7

boundaries: what a bubble, feed card, expanded view and mod mail show when a message cannot be opened
what the edit box is pre-filled with
the status of a decrypt, against the text that accompanies it

prior_ledgers_read: 04cf8a171 -- the review immediately before this one. It found this defect, proved it, recorded it in its notes and deferred it for a copy decision. This pass looked for that copy and found it already existed, so the deferral was wrong.
ba2c83dd4 and 6e346b3fd -- read for anything about display of failed decrypts; neither records one.
notes: The previous review deferred this on the grounds that fixing it needed a decision about what a bubble should say. That was wrong, and the way to find out took one grep: SearchResultsPage already answers exactly this, for exactly these two statuses, with t(messages.encrypted). The lesson is that "this needs a product decision" is itself a claim to check, not a reason to stop.

H3 by module name is not enough. The first enumeration missed CompactPostCard.decrypt.test.tsx, which renders a consumer of the changed hook without importing it. Enumerate by CONSUMER as well as by module.
decryptMessageForEdit was exported so its refusal could be controlled. Exporting for testability was the smaller price than leaving the more dangerous half of the finding without a control.

instruments.evidence: Three files. useDecryptedContent stops publishing the text of a failed decrypt; MessagesPage stops handing that text to the edit box and the history modal. The boundary is what a reader sees when a message cannot be opened.
Read 04cf8a171 -- the review immediately before this one, which FOUND this defect, recorded it in its notes and deferred it for a copy decision. That deferral is what this pass overturned.

The artifact is the string a consumer receives. Printed it by calling decryptForDisplay with an unavailable key: status failed, text identical to the sealed envelope. Printed again after the fix through the control, whose failure names both values side by side.
Four consumers render this string: the conversation bubble, the feed card, the expanded view and mod mail. All four now receive the label instead of the envelope, because all four read the same hook.

instruments.why: No handler changed.
No query, migration or stored row changed.

instruments.evidence: The label is not a new literal: it is t('messages.encrypted'), the same key SearchResultsPage already uses for the same two statuses.
decryptMessageForEdit changed shape from Promise<string> to Promise<string | null>, and both call sites were updated. tsc enforces that there is no third caller.
Two implementations of one rule existed: SearchResultsPage handled failed and no-keys, the shared hook did not. They now agree, and the hook is the one place the four display consumers read.
No external contract; the producer is decryptForDisplay in the same module.

instruments.why: No struct field added.

instruments.evidence: The reader broken is the status check itself. Both controls revert it and both tests fail with real assertions that print the ciphertext they were handed.

instruments.why: The fixtures are sealed envelopes of the shape the sender writes; the group vector file supplies the real one.

instruments.evidence: A message that really opens still shows its text: asserted for the group vector with the key present, and for a plaintext message through the edit helper.
The input that must be refused is a sealed envelope with no key. Refused in both places.
The boundary is the status: decrypted and not-encrypted pass, failed and no-keys are labelled. All four are exercised.
Found the first finding. SearchResultsPage carried the defence -- label the two unreadable statuses rather than print their text -- and the shared hook did not, though four surfaces depend on it.
No branch became unreachable. The new branch is reached by a test, and the old one still carries decrypted and not-encrypted.
Nothing is swallowed. The refusal is visible: the editor says so, the history modal says so, the bubble says so.

instruments.why: No flag gates these paths.

instruments.evidence: The words exist once, in the locale file, and both call sites use the key rather than a second literal.

Found the second finding. Having fixed the hook, asked who else consumes result.text without its status: PinnedMessagesBar was already correct, SearchResultsPage was the model, and decryptMessageForEdit was not -- the worst of the three, because its consumer is an edit box.

instruments.why: No goroutine or shared mutable state.
No transaction or queue work.
No migration.
Nothing persisted; the change is what a string says.

instruments.evidence: Two controls, both replayed by hand after their commits. The bubble control fails with expected {"v":1,"k":1,...} to be "End-to-end encrypted"; the edit control fails with expected {"v":1,"k":3,...} to be null. Real assertions, and both files still compile with the patch applied.
Both tests run inside their suites rather than only when named, and both suites are in the default vitest include.
tsc -b 0, eslint 0, prettier 0, i18n check and guard clean. The guard matters here because the fix adds translated strings: alertCalls stays 0, because the alert uses t().

Both findings came from instruments already on the list, E1 and E6. The one lesson worth keeping is recorded in the notes: H3 by module name misses a test that renders a consumer without importing the module.

instruments.why: Nothing here crosses into a model, provider or other system. The artifact is a string, and the test asserts it exactly -- including the real English wording, which the control proved by printing "End-to-end encrypted" in its failure.
Nothing starts early.

instruments.evidence: Each guard was fed the thing it refuses -- a sealed envelope with no key -- and refused it.

instruments.why: No layout changed.
No process-wide lazy state.

instruments.evidence: Counted: 58 passed and 1 pre-existing skip across the 7-suite H3 set; the skip is a MessagesPage swipe test named in the output.
Not a plan phase. This is the review of G4a-1 finding a defect outside it and fixing it, which the skill asks for.

instruments.why: No side effect has two entry points here.
No overlay changed.

instruments.evidence: Enumerated twice. The first grep, by module name, missed CompactPostCard.decrypt.test.tsx, which renders a consumer without ever naming the hook. Re-enumerated by CONSUMER name and found three more suites. All 7 ran.

instruments.why: Nothing can cover or redirect the app.
No shared Go fixture or route registry.

instruments.evidence: No existing control targets useDecryptedContent.ts or MessagesPage.tsx; checked by grep over every patch in .review/controls. The two added here were replayed after their own commits.

instruments.why: No resource is acquired after an await by the changed code.
No unmount cleanup changed; the hook still cancels with a local flag.

findings.summary: useDecryptedContent published result.text whatever the status, and the text of a failed decrypt is the ciphertext. A group message whose key version the reader never received rendered as a raw sealed envelope in the conversation, the feed card, the expanded view and mod mail.

control.observed: With the fix reverted the test fails: AssertionError: expected '{"v":1,"k":1,"iv":"AAECAwQFBgcICQoL",...' to be 'End-to-end encrypted'. The failure prints the defect itself.

findings.summary: decryptMessageForEdit returned the text regardless of status, so the edit box could open pre-filled with a sealed envelope. Saving that would replace the message with its own ciphertext as plaintext, and the history modal showed the same envelope.

tests: src/pages/__tests__/MessagesPage.test.tsx -t "refuses a message it could not open"
control.observed: With the fix reverted the test fails: AssertionError: expected '{"v":1,"k":3,"iv":"AAECAwQFBgcICQoL",...' to be null.

instruments.evidence: The new code is a status branch in the hook, a null return in the edit helper, an export, and two tests.
No prior ledger records a fix here; 04cf8a171 recorded the defect and deferred it.
The string each consumer receives was printed once before the fix and once through each control after it. Both controls print the envelope beside the expected value.

Checked what each of the four consumers does with the new value. CompactPostCard returns null on an empty preview, and the label is not empty, so a message that could not be opened now renders the label where it previously rendered the envelope. Nothing renders differently for a message that opens.

instruments.why: Unchanged from pass 1: No handler changed.
Unchanged from pass 1: No query, migration or stored row changed.

instruments.evidence: One key, used by two call sites and already used by a third.
Promise<string | null> is enforced by tsc at both call sites; there is no third.
The hook and SearchResultsPage now answer the same question the same way.
No external contract.

instruments.why: Unchanged from pass 1: No struct field added.

instruments.evidence: Both controls break the reader and both fail as tests.

instruments.why: Unchanged from pass 1: The fixtures are sealed envelopes of the shape the sender writes; the group vector file supplies the real one.

instruments.evidence: A message that opens still shows its text, asserted in both suites.
A sealed envelope with no key is refused in both places.
All four statuses are exercised across the two suites.
The defence SearchResultsPage carried is now carried by the shared hook as well.
Asked whether labelling breaks a legacy plaintext message read on a device with no keys. It does not: such a message is not-encrypted, not no-keys, so it never reaches the new branch.
Every refusal is visible to the person who triggered it.

instruments.why: Unchanged from pass 1: No flag gates these paths.

instruments.evidence: One key, one place.

Swept the remaining consumers of decryptForDisplay a second time. PinnedMessagesBar takes text only when decrypted. SearchResultsPage labels. The conversation-search path omits failed and deliberately shows the stored value for no-keys, with a comment from an earlier review explaining why -- inspected and left alone rather than contradicting a recorded decision on no evidence.
